then.text: How's my wee Jamlet getting on? Feed it oranges. Not jam. It finds that confusing.

else.text: Marmalade for the Discovery? Scott's men took Dundee marmalade to the Antarctic, you know. It goes well with a frozen biscuit.
Here, two jars, sealed tight. Now, hold still, there's something in the crate. Oh! It's one of the wee jam ones. It must have climbed in for the peel.
It's taken a shine to you. Keep it. It's very sticky, very loyal, and it'll grow into a proper crock one day.
The Keillers sold marmalade from Dundee from the 1790s. Folk say Janet Keiller invented it with a cheap shipload of Seville oranges. Lovely story. Marmalade's older, though. Don't tell the tourists.
The trick is the peel: thick-cut, bitter and sweet. The Keillers put their spare peel into a fruit cake, and that's how Dundee cake got famous. Waste not.
